title: mine evidence to extend US_STATES for India
headline: India's state table needs NO extension: all 34 two-letter state codes present in India addresses resolve via the self-map loop (3,188,831/3,188,831 = 100.0%), and every IN_STATES full name that occurs is present. The real gap is ADDR_CANON_COMMON vocabulary: 1,118 distinct India address words worth 27,883,154 listed occurrences (28.6% of India address-token mass) have no entry. Two NEW defects found outside the India tables: LEET corrupts ordinals in the name field (France 1,111 occurrences = 20.9% of France's mixed name tokens), and France direction words are unhandled with 'est' actively mis-mapped to 'estate' (154,955 occurrences).

F6_new_defect_france_direction_words.code_ref: ADDR_CANON_FR normalize.py:199-214; canon built at normalize.py:321
F6_new_defect_france_direction_words.root_cause: 'est' is not in the removal tuple, so ADDR_CANON_COMMON['est']='estate' (normalize.py:186) survives into the French canon
F6_new_defect_france_direction_words.note: nord is a FR_REGIONS key -> hdf, so it resolves as a whole-component state but is never canonicalised as a token inside a longer component

gaps: Token denominators are lower bounds: build_profile.py prunes count<=1 every 8 chunks and truncates to TOPN=4000, so 28.6% is an upper bound on the unhandled share
No component-level field, so token co-occurrence cannot be proven; F4 pairing claims are LIKELY not CONFIRMED except where the existing table asserts the relationship
No co-occurrence counts of any kind; only marginal token frequencies are derivable
The identity of the 337 comma-free rows is unknown (no address text in the profile)
All France rows are in test_s{1,2,3}; no France training data exists to validate against
self_corrections: First LEET probe tested 'd in LEET' on a str.maketrans dict (ordinal keys) and wrongly concluded all digits were unmapped. Reading actual LEET keys [36,48,49,51,52,53,54,55,56,64] = '$01345678@' showed only 2 and 9 are unmapped and the real defect is over-eager mapping of 1 and 3.
